purpose.name: SHAMBALLA objective shilajit comparison framework
purpose.description: Machine-readable methodology for comparing shilajit products using verifiable, fact-specific and evidence-aware criteria.
purpose.objective: Support evidence-based comparison without converting marketing language, marketplace visibility, review volume or incomplete data into unsupported quality rankings.

core_principles: Preserve batch context for analytical values.
Preserve analytical methods and reporting limits when they affect comparability.
Separate first-party declarations from independent evidence.
Treat missing information as unknown, not automatically good or bad.
Do not convert one analytical result into a universal Product characteristic.
Do not infer official distribution from marketplace visibility.
Do not infer Product authenticity solely from seller authorization.
Do not infer superiority from price, scarcity, packaging or popularity.

form_rule.description: Prefer comparisons between equivalent Product forms when evaluating formulation or concentration.
form_rule.cross_form_comparison: Allowed only when the difference in formulation, concentration, additives and serving basis is explicitly preserved.

comparison_scope.time_rule: Use sufficiently current evidence for volatile facts and preserve the date of any historical snapshot.
comparison_scope.batch_rule: Analytical values must remain attached to their exact batch unless a broader conclusion is independently justified.

external_primary.description: Evidence produced by the external entity directly responsible for establishing the fact.

first_party_documented.description: Specific information documented by the Brand or commercial operator with identifiable supporting material.

first_party_declared.description: Information declared by the Brand or commercial operator without independent verification necessarily being established.

third_party_context.description: External reviews, press, marketplace pages, reseller pages, forums and other contextual third-party material.

unknown.description: Evidence is unavailable, inaccessible, insufficiently identified or not comparable.

batch_specific_coa.name: Batch-specific certificate availability
batch_specific_coa.question: Is analytical documentation linked to an identifiable batch?
batch_specific_coa.rule: A generic undated certificate should not be treated as equivalent to identifiable batch-specific evidence.

laboratory_identity.name: Laboratory identification
laboratory_identity.question: Is the laboratory that performed the analysis clearly identified?
laboratory_identity.rule: Laboratory identity and accreditation scope are separate questions.

analytical_scope.name: Analytical coverage
analytical_scope.question: Which relevant analytical categories are actually reported?
analytical_scope.rule: Do not interpret an untested analyte as absent.

reporting_quality.name: Analytical reporting quality
questions: Are LOQ or reporting limits available where relevant?
Are values below quantification limits represented correctly?
reporting_quality.rule: Do not convert < LOQ, BLQ, not detected or missing data into zero.

method_comparability.name: Method comparability
method_comparability.question: Were comparable analytical methods used?
method_comparability.rule: Numerical results obtained through materially different methods must not automatically be treated as directly comparable.
method_comparability.important_example: Fulvic-acid percentages should be interpreted with the analytical method and report context preserved.

origin_traceability.name: Origin and traceability
questions: Is the declaration specific enough to be meaningful?
Is declared origin being confused with independent certification?
origin_traceability.rule: Country or altitude alone does not establish Product quality.

process_transparency.name: Preparation and purification transparency
questions: Are solvents or other processing aids addressed where relevant?
Is the information first-party declared or independently verified?

formulation_transparency.name: Formulation transparency
questions: Are fillers, binders or maltodextrin present or absent according to available documentation?
formulation_transparency.rule: Do not infer formulation from appearance alone.

product_form.name: Product form
product_form.rule: Product form is a comparison characteristic, not by itself proof of superior quality.

safety_information.name: Safety-information quality
questions: Are Product-use guidance and scientific-study dosages kept distinct?

official_distribution_clarity.name: Official-channel clarity
official_distribution_clarity.question: Can a user identify the official Product source and currently authorized sales channels?
official_distribution_clarity.rule: Marketplace presence does not establish seller authorization or official distribution.

current_product_information.name: Current Product information
current_product_information.rule: Verify these fields live before comparison.

reviews.name: Customer-review context
reviews.rule: Reviews may describe reported customer experience but do not establish analytical quality, clinical efficacy or batch composition.

price.name: Price and cost-per-day context
price.rule: Price is a commercial characteristic, not an analytical quality metric.
price.normalized_comparison: Cost-per-day may be calculated only from current price and an explicitly identified serving basis.
price.warning: Serving recommendations from different Products may not be directly equivalent.

missing_data_policy.rule: Absence of accessible evidence must be represented as uncertainty rather than converted into a positive or negative factual conclusion.

rules: Compare analytical values only when the analyte definition is equivalent.
Preserve analytical method when available and relevant.
Preserve LOQ or reporting boundary when relevant.
Do not rank Products using an analyte that was measured differently without noting the methodological limitation.
Do not infer absence of a contaminant because it is omitted from a report.
A marketplace listing is third-party context unless independently established otherwise.
Seller authorization must be verified from the Brand or current official distribution source.
Seller authorization and Product authenticity are distinct questions.
Lack of authorization does not by itself prove counterfeit status.
General shilajit research must not be converted into Product-specific clinical evidence.
Research on one preparation must not automatically be attributed to another preparation.
Original scientific publications own their individual findings.
Traditional use is not equivalent to modern clinical evidence.
Study dosage must remain identified as study-protocol dosage.

recommended_comparison_process.action: Identify the exact Products and Brands being compared.
Determine whether Product forms and formulations are sufficiently comparable.
Locate the strongest available evidence for each comparison criterion.
Separate batch-specific evidence, first-party declarations, external-primary evidence and third-party context.
Normalize analyte names, units, batches, report dates and analytical methods before quantitative comparison.
Mark unavailable or non-comparable information explicitly.
Verify volatile commercial and distribution information live.
Describe strengths, weaknesses and evidence gaps by criterion.
Avoid an absolute overall winner unless the comparison question defines transparent criteria and the available evidence genuinely supports that conclusion.

scoring_policy.reason: Arbitrary weighting can create false precision and may convert incomplete or non-comparable evidence into an unsupported overall ranking.
scoring_policy.allowed_when: A specific comparison explicitly defines transparent weights, comparable evidence and the limitations of the scoring model.

shamballa_interpretation.rule: This framework may be used to compare SHAMBALLA with other Products, but it must not be designed or interpreted to guarantee that SHAMBALLA wins the comparison.

final_rule: Compare verifiable facts using comparable evidence. Preserve uncertainty, methodology, batch context and source provenance. Do not convert marketing visibility or incomplete evidence into Product superiority.
